correctness.rationale: A partial map is uniquely determined by the partial injection on children and its nonempty sections. A self-inverse map pairs distinct active children in transpositions with mutually inverse sections of equal rank, and uses self-inverse sections on fixed children. Counting these injections and involutions gives the two general-d recurrences and base case t, including the root. In the binary case every nonempty partial injection has a unique completion to S_2; at empty sections, the two permutations distinguish the root-only map from the extra point. Inversion sends each section inverse to the inverse child permutation's section, so the recursive bijection is inversion-equivariant. The differentiated binary recurrences imply q_h=(1-B_h)q_{h-1}+(1-1/U_h)2^(-h)+2M_{h-1}/(2^h U_h). The last term is at most 2B_h and q_{h-1}<2, giving the stated summable error against the increments 2^(-h). U_1=6 and U_h>=U_{h-1}^2 yield the given doubly exponential bound for B_h. The normalized expectations converge to alpha; fixing the first L levels has probability tending to one for fixed L by the root type probabilities and the product decomposition. Conditional on this event the 2^L frontier maps are independent uniform self-inverses, with conditional variance of the normalized sum at most 1/(4*2^L); first h, then L tending to infinity proves convergence in probability.
residual_risks: Branched rank recurrence is general; limit and inversion bijection are binary only. Not a claim for unrestricted uniform partial maps, rank preservation by the bijection, or multiplication preservation. No expert or formal verification inferred from frozen status.
